_comment: Internationalization framework — metric (m³) stem-volume equations for the European paradigm. Laasasenaho (1982) Nordic coefficients are VERIFIED against the R package lmfor (predvol); see docs/volume-standards-research.md §B. The German form-factor record is a labelled APPROXIMATION (§C). Seeded alongside the US PNW set; referenced by country-prefixed species a metric cruiser assigns. Korea is intentionally absent — its official NIFoS coefficients are pending, so no Korean equation is fabricated.

equations.sourceCitation: Laasasenaho, J. 1982. Taper curve and volume functions for pine, spruce and birch. Comm. Inst. For. Fenn. 108. Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris). Coefficients verified via R lmfor::predvol.
Laasasenaho (1982). Norway spruce (Picea abies). Coefficients verified via R lmfor::predvol.
Laasasenaho (1982). Silver birch (Betula pendula); downy birch (B. pubescens) shares these coefficients in the lmfor implementation. Verified via R lmfor::predvol.
Generic whole-tree form factor V=g·h·f, f≈0.50 (0.45–0.55). APPROXIMATION — Germany's production standard is the BDAT taper program (no short closed form). AWF-Wiki, Univ. Göttingen, 'Stem shape'.
